# PDF Tools, packaged as an Agent Plugin

This repository is a distribution channel, not a source repository. It holds a prebuilt, installable [Agent Plugins 1.0.0](https://agent-plugins.org) build of [PDF Tools](https://github.com/Open-Document-Alliance/PDF-Tools) so that agent clients can install it directly.

**All development happens in [Open-Document-Alliance/PDF-Tools](https://github.com/Open-Document-Alliance/PDF-Tools).** Everything under `plugins/` here is generated by `npm run build:plugin` in that repository. Do not edit it by hand; changes will be overwritten on the next release.

## Install

```bash
codex plugin marketplace add Open-Document-Alliance/pdf-tools-plugin
codex plugin add pdf-tools@open-document-alliance
```

Other Agent Plugins clients that accept a Git marketplace should work the same way, though only the Codex CLI has been verified so far.

## First run: it starts with access to nothing

PDF Tools reads and writes files on your machine, so it will not touch a folder you have not named.

Agent Plugins deliberately defines no user-configuration mechanism, so there is nowhere for a host to ask you which folders to allow. Rather than guess, this plugin starts with an empty allow list and tells you where to fix that. On first run it writes a config file under the plugin's data directory, and every refusal names the exact path:

```json
{
  "directories": [],
  "configured": false,
  "source": "none",
  "config_path": ".../plugins/data/agent-plugins/<id>/config.json"
}
```

Open that file, list your folders under `allowedDirectories`, and restart the server:

```json
{
  "allowedDirectories": ["/Users/you/Documents", "/Users/you/Desktop"]
}
```

This is the intended behavior, not a bug. Earlier versions of PDF Tools silently fell back to Documents, Downloads and Desktop when a host supplied no configuration. On the plugin path that fallback would have applied to every install, because no host can configure it. It was removed in v0.10.0.

## What is inside

| Path | What it is |
|---|---|
| `plugin.json` | The Agent Plugins manifest |
| `mcp.json` | Declares the `pdf-tools` stdio server, launched via `${PLUGIN_ROOT}` |
| `server/` | The MCP server |
| `skills/` | The evidence-first PDF workflow skill |
| `dist-ui/` | The interactive viewer, served as an MCP Apps resource |
| `node_modules/` | Vendored dependencies |

Dependencies are committed on purpose. Agent Plugins defines no install or build lifecycle, so a plugin has to arrive complete. Most of the size is `@napi-rs/canvas`, which ships a native rendering binary for each supported platform so that page rasterization works without a compiler on the user's machine.

## Status

Alpha. The build installs and serves tools on the Codex CLI. It has not been verified on Cursor, VS Code, GitHub Copilot, Kiro, or the ChatGPT desktop app, and the Agent Plugins specification defines no registry, so each client resolves marketplaces its own way.

The interactive viewer is built on MCP Apps and should render on hosts that support that extension, but it has not yet been observed rendering on a non-Anthropic host.

For Claude Desktop, install the `.mcpb` from the [PDF Tools releases](https://github.com/Open-Document-Alliance/PDF-Tools/releases) instead. It is the better-tested path and supports folder configuration through the app's own settings.
